meta.author: Iris Meng

executive_summary.headline: Enter Vietnam Q3 2026 via $40M JV with Partner X for projected 3.2x return
bullets: Vietnam offers Southeast Asia's fastest middle-class spending growth at 7% CAGR through 2030
JV structure cuts capital-at-risk by ~60% versus greenfield with a six-month launch window
Three local partners screened on distribution, regulatory, and category fit; Partner X recommended

slides.action_title: SEA middle-class spending reaches $2.8T by 2030, with Vietnam and Indonesia driving 70% of growth
slides.footnote: Excludes Singapore. Middle class defined as households earning $11k to $110k per year in PPP terms.
slides.source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, 2024; McKinsey Global Institute, Asia 2030, 2024

slides.action_title: Acme's portfolio fits Vietnam's three fastest-growing categories with no Western incumbent
bullets: Premium dairy: 12% CAGR through 2030, fragmented competition, no dominant Western brand at the premium tier
Health and wellness: 9% CAGR, regulatory environment increasingly favorable to imported nutraceuticals
Convenience foods: 8% CAGR, modern trade penetration tripling by 2030 via 7-Eleven and GS25 expansion
slides.source: Euromonitor Vietnam Consumer Outlook, 2024; Acme internal portfolio analysis, 2025

slides.action_title: JV beats greenfield and acquisition on capital risk, speed, and retained operational control

left.text: Capital-at-risk: $40M JV vs $80M greenfield vs $120M+ acquisition
Regulatory clearance in 4 to 6 months via partner's existing licenses
Distribution access from day one through partner's 12,000-store network

right.text: Six-month launch versus 24 months greenfield build-out
Local hiring infrastructure already in place
Brand localization can begin during negotiation, not after close

slides.action_title: Partner X leads on distribution, regulatory, and category fit; capex governance is the only gap
slides.footnote: Capex governance reflects Partner X's preference for unanimous-consent thresholds; counterproposal in negotiation.

recommendations.headline: Approve $40M for the Vietnam JV with Partner X, targeting Q3 2026 launch

actions.action: Finalize term sheet with Partner X by 2026-08, including capex governance framework
Stand up JV operations team and 24-month launch plan by 2026-09
Brand localization, trade marketing plan, and category lead hires by 2026-09
Regulatory submission via partner's licenses, IP transfer agreements by 2026-08
actions.outcome: Regulatory and IP cleared for launch

appendix.action_title: Vietnam JV reaches breakeven month 14, $180M revenue and 18% EBITDA margin by Year 5
appendix.footnote: Base case. Sensitivity range +/- 25% on Year 5 revenue; refer to corporate development model.

appendix.action_title: Partner X due diligence validates distribution and regulatory; capex governance is the only open issue
bullets: Distribution: 12,000 stores across 63 provinces, modern and traditional trade balance of 60/40, validated against POS data
Regulatory: holds nine of the eleven category licenses Acme requires; remaining two are partner-application-eligible
Capex governance: Partner X prefers unanimous-consent for capex over $5M; Acme counterproposal sets threshold at $15M
Financial: audited financials reviewed by Big Four; net leverage 1.8x, no covenant issues
appendix.source: Acme partner due diligence and external auditor review, 2025
